hooks: Some of the wildest scenes in GTA 6's first trailer look just like real viral videos.

scenes.narration: Some of the wildest scenes in GTA 6's first trailer look just like real viral videos.
When the trailer dropped in December 2023, fans started matching its moments to real viral videos from Florida.
Remember the woman dancing on top of a car?
Know Your Meme traced it to a real clip from Miami's MacArthur Causeway, during spring break 2017.
Then there's the man hauling a huge alligator out of a backyard pool.
A real trapper did exactly that, and a Florida news station filmed it in 2019.
And the alligator wandering into a store? A real one walked into a Florida Walmart back in 2013.
Even dirt bike crews racing around South Florida made the local news.
Rockstar has never said which clips inspired these scenes.
But next time GTA 6 feels way over the top, remember that real Florida got there first.
What's the craziest Florida story you've ever heard?

facts.claim: Know Your Meme (6 Dec 2023) matched GTA VI trailer moments to real Florida videos: a woman twerking on a car on Miami's MacArthur Causeway during spring break (March 2017); a trapper dragging a large alligator out of a pool (WPBF 25 News, April 2019); an alligator at a Florida Walmart (Sky News, October 2013); ATVs and dirt bikes racing in South Florida (NBC 6, February 2023).
Rockstar has not confirmed which real clips inspired the trailer.

script.title: GTA 6 still isn't on PC. Here's why
hooks: GTA 6 is finally out, but PC players still can't play it.

scenes.narration: GTA 6 is finally out, but PC players still can't play it.
It launched on November 19th on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only.
And Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC date.
So why make PC players wait?
Take-Two's boss, Strauss Zelnick, says Rockstar always starts on console.
In his words, the core audience has to "be served first and best."
And if history is any guide, PC players know this wait well.
GTA 5 came out on consoles in September 2013, and only reached PC in April 2015.
Red Dead Redemption 2 waited just over a year for its PC version.
So if history repeats, PC players could be waiting a year or more.
Rockstar hasn't said that, but the pattern is hard to ignore.
PC players, would you wait, or buy a console just for GTA 6?

script.title: The GTA 5 record GTA 6 has to beat
hooks: GTA 6 is finally out, and it's chasing one of the biggest records in entertainment.

scenes.narration: GTA 6 is finally out, and it's chasing one of the biggest records in entertainment.
Back in 2013, GTA 5 made over eight hundred million dollars in its first twenty-four hours.
It also sold more than eleven million copies on that first day.
Three days later, it passed one billion dollars.
Guinness World Records called it the fastest entertainment product ever to make a billion dollars.
That means it beat every movie, album and game that came before it.
So can GTA 6 beat that?
Take-Two hasn't shared a single sales number yet.
But earlier this month, the company said pre-orders were "tracking far above our initial expectations."

Some also say the story's pacing sags in places.
Reviewers also praise how packed and detailed the game's world feels.
One roundup calls it the most reactive city Rockstar has built.
Thirteen years after GTA 5, the critics say the wait was worth it.
So is 99 too high, or does GTA 6 really deserve it?

scenes.narration: When GTA 6 unlocked this week, almost eight million people watched other people play it, all at once.

That's the biggest game launch it has ever recorded.
The old launch record was Valorant's closed beta in 2020, with about 1.7 million.
GTA 6 pulled in more than four times that.
On Twitch alone, it peaked at 3.31 million.
That beat the Twitch record for any game, set by League of Legends in 2022.
In one day, Twitch viewers watched thirty-six million hours of it.
Even the internet felt it: an internet exchange called DE-CIX set a traffic record.
So has anything drawn a bigger crowd on Twitch? Just one thing.
A 2025 boxing night called La Velada, with 9.68 million.
So by Streams Charts' count, only a boxing night has ever beaten it on Twitch.
Were you playing it, or watching someone play it?

facts.claim: Streams Charts (preliminary): GTA 6 peaked at more than 7.91 million concurrent viewers across livestreaming platforms, the biggest game launch ever (all platforms); 3.31 million on Twitch, overtaking League of Legends (3,111,143, T1-DRX Worlds 2022 final), the previous gaming record; 36,060,208 Twitch hours watched in one day, the most by a game; about 4.6 times Valorant's closed beta; La Velada (2025 boxing event) still holds Twitch's overall record with 9.68 million.

script.title: GTA 6 runs best on one console. Here's which
hooks: On the wrong console, GTA 6 can drop to around twenty frames a second.

scenes.narration: On the wrong console, GTA 6 can drop to around twenty frames a second.
Digital Foundry tested them all. First, the bad news.
Every console aims for thirty frames a second. There's no sixty frames mode.
Rockstar told Kotaku the consoles can't run its simulation any faster.
So which one holds thirty best?
Last place: the Xbox Series S.
It runs at just 720p, and in big shootouts it falls to around twenty.
The base PS5 and Series X sit in the middle, both at 1440p.
Blow up enough cars, and the PS5 dips to twenty-three.
The Series X dips a bit lower, but on a 120 hertz VRR TV, those dips feel smoother.
And the winner is the PS5 Pro.
It's the only one with ray-traced shadows, and it looks close to native 4K.
On the Pro, Digital Foundry saw no drops in fifty hours of normal play.
PlayStation or Xbox: which side are you on? Follow for more GTA 6 tips.

facts.claim: Digital Foundry (18 Nov 2026): every version targets 30 fps, no 40/60 fps mode; PS5 Pro 1440p internal with PSSR to a near-4K image, the only version with ray-traced shadows, brief drops to ~24 fps only in an explosion-heavy test, ranked best; base PS5 and Series X 1440p internal, spatially upscaled; Series X dips a touch below PS5 (~20-22 fps worst) with 120 Hz VRR and LFC smoothing dips on a compatible TV; Series S 720p with FSR to ~1080p, 'around 20 FPS or lower' in the heaviest action, a 'distant fourth'.
Base PS5 dips as low as 23 fps when blowing up vehicles; DF saw no dips in normal play over 50+ hours on PS5 Pro; DF called the Pro 'the best way to play this game by far'.
Rockstar's Marc Chambers to Kotaku (18 Nov 2026): the hardware 'is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates'.

script.description:
Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 on PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S. All aim for 30 fps; one holds it best, one struggles.
Sources: Digital Foundry (via GTA BOOM, AltChar, Endgame Tools), Kotaku.

He told Bloomberg: "You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer."
Bloomberg's Jason Schreier has also reported that the online part is expected in 2027.
Rockstar hasn't confirmed that.
Meanwhile, Take-Two says it will keep supporting GTA Online on GTA 5.

hooks: GTA 6 isn't the first time Rockstar has taken us to Vice City.

scenes.narration: GTA 6 isn't the first time Rockstar has taken us to Vice City.
The first trip was GTA Vice City, which came out in October 2002 on the PlayStation 2.
It was set in 1986, in a city based heavily on Miami.
You played as gangster Tommy Vercetti, voiced by the actor Ray Liotta.
It was a huge hit, with over seventeen and a half million copies sold.
It was one of the PlayStation 2's best-selling games.
